title: His ideal recording team and setting
summary: He would use Teddy Charles, Teo Macero and Les Paul and record in Columbia's church studio with unlimited time.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: If you had the chance to -- if somebody gave you a grant, to make some records, and you'd be in charge of the whole operation in terms of picking the label, picking the studio, the A&R, the engineer, what would you do?
Tio Macero, I'd get Teddy Charles for
I'd get Tio Becelle for engineer, e macro I'd get Les Paul for the engineer.
I'd get some guy who knows electronic things. I'd try to get the guy who's in Columbia.
His last name, I think, is Plaut, P-l-a-u-t. I'm not sure that Fred is his first name.
And where would you do it?
Oh, on 30th Street or something like that.
With as much time as was needed, right?
Yeah. I don't know these studios (unintelligible), you know about those studios?
They lived for three or four months there.
That seems to be too much time. I've heard something like that, but it seems to me you get so--
They got sauna baths, (inaudible) food, little kitchens.
